title: Apple researchers introduce Normalizing Trajectory Models
excerpt: The new method models reverse steps as conditional normalizing flows to maintain exact likelihood training in image generation.
bodyHtml:
Apple researchers announced the development of Normalizing Trajectory Models (NTM) on October 8, 2026. The method addresses diffusion-based models, which decompose sampling into many small Gaussian denoising steps, an assumption that breaks down when generation is compressed to a few coarse transitions.

NTM models each reverse step as an expressive conditional normalizing flow with exact likelihood training. Architecturally, NTM combines shallow invertible blocks within each step with a deep parallel predictor across the trajectory, forming an end-to-end network trainable from scratch or initializable from pretrained flow-matching models.

The model's exact trajectory likelihood enables self-distillation. A lightweight denoiser trained on the score function induced by the model itself produces high-quality samples in four steps. On text-to-image benchmarks, NTM matches or outperforms strong image generation baselines in just four sampling steps while uniquely retaining exact likelihood over the generative trajectory.
